correctness.rationale: Exact graph-adjacency modules follow from the truncated dyadic group algebra and the complete-clique idempotent/square-zero parity split. The change c=a+b in F_q[a,b]/(a^L,b^2) is invertible because L is a power of two; it yields the even-clique Jordan lengths. Eliminating the nilpotent adjacency parameter in X^2+(beta+a)X+1=0 proves the full cyclic wave modules, including split cyclotomic polynomials over extension fields. GCD with X^t-1 gives every exact fixed-space dimension. Möbius inversion and strict monotonicity prove all stated primitive periods. Two provided programs pass 438 binary rank comparisons and direct neighbor update checks; finite experiments are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The tested statement is the complete labelled fixed-time and primitive-orbit census, with exact two-row cyclic modules, for the natural family C_(2^r) Cartesian K_m, r>=3. The inspected older second-order constructions give reversibility and special one-dimensional seed growth but not these finite graph modules. Published records found by the actual searches concern different update rules or graphs. A known mixed-Hamming wave theorem covers the excluded four-cycle base case; a known dyadic-hypertorus wave theorem covers products solely of dyadic cycles, not a clique-fiber cylinder with r>=3. No checked theorem implies the full stated module or formula, although unindexed historical results remain a genuine priority risk. A closer dyadic first-order cyclic precursor, Tadaki (1994), has also been inspected in full; its rule-90 nilpotence is acknowledged as background but does not imply the clique-fiber reversible-wave temporal census.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unexamined historical studies of binary reversible waves may contain an equivalent clique-cylinder calculation.

value.rationale: The question asks a natural complete invariant, namely the temporal-orbit population distribution of a reversible graph wave on an infinite family of labelled clique-fiber cylinders. An exact, unbounded dyadic clock bifurcates by clique parity, and the full cyclic module gives all fixed populations over every finite characteristic-two field. It is structurally motivated by the interaction of cycle nilpotence and clique idempotence, not a renamed parameter or isolated small calculation.
